original.full_text: The era of the 'digital-only' AI experiment is officially over. NVIDIA’s deepening partnership with Doosan isn't just a tech headline; it is the death knell for passive industrial processes. We are moving into the age of Physical AI, where heavy machinery, robotics, and digital twins synchronize to operate autonomous factory floors. Locally, this hits hard: Houston’s manufacturing and energy sectors currently face a labor-to-production efficiency gap that traditional automation hasn't bridged. At Amplify Intelligence, we are tracking how this convergence will force a total redesign of the industrial plant. The data is clear: companies integrating real-time robotics and digital twins report up to a 25% increase in operational throughput. Why does this matter for the C-suite? Because the hardware stack is finally catching up to the software. If you're still viewing AI as a tool for drafting emails or summarizing meeting notes, you are ignoring the tectonic shift happening in the physical world. Leon Coe here—I’ve been guiding Houston firms through these infrastructure pivots, and the feedback is consistent: Those who integrate physical AI models into their supply chains today will hold the competitive high ground for the next decade. The hardware has evolved, and the software has matured; the only remaining variable is your execution strategy. Is your current industrial infrastructure capable of sustaining a move toward autonomous physical AI, or is your hardware already five years behind?

Here in Houston, this matters for a specific reason: our energy and manufacturing sectors are still struggling to close the gap between labor availability and production targets. Traditional automation wasn't enough, but hardware is finally catching up to the software. At Amplify Intelligence, we’re seeing firms report a 25% jump in throughput just by plugging in real-time robotics. If you're still treating AI as a glorified chatbot for meeting minutes, you’re missing the shift happening on the factory floor.
